integrity: Vertex-edge domination is reduced exactly to the condition that the selected closed neighborhood is a vertex cover. Every two-vertex total candidate either fails totality or leaves the opposite deleted-matching endpoints joined by an uncovered edge. Every three-vertex candidate of the stated form has no selected isolate and leaves at most one vertex outside its closed neighborhood. The total condition then forces the three matching indices to be distinct, yielding the complete classification.
scientific_limitations: The theorem treats balanced crown graphs and not arbitrary matching deletions from complete bipartite graphs.
Finite exhaustive verification covers n from three through eight and is corroborative only.
The 2021 chain-graph algorithmic article was accessible through its abstract and metadata rather than full article text.
A differently phrased or non-indexed crown treatment may exist.
title: Minimum total vertex-edge dominating sets of crown graphs
